reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern exhibits a robust quasi-periodic square-wave–like motif with a fundamental period of ~83 points, as confirmed by the dataset metadata and consistent across all candidates. Each cycle contains a sharp upward step (rise time ≤2 points), a flat plateau lasting ~20–30 points, a sharp downward step (fall time ≤2 points), and a flat trough lasting ~20–30 points—forming a symmetric duty cycle (~50%). Plateau levels are stable near +0.75 to +1.05 (robust standardized) and troughs near −0.75 to −0.5, with median exactly 0.0 due to robust standardization. Amplitude (90th percentile range) is tightly bounded between ~1.44 and 1.78, indicating low amplitude variability. Noise manifests as small high-frequency spikes (±0.1–0.2) superimposed on plateaus/troughs, especially in longer windows (3P and 5P), but never disrupts the core step-plateau morphology. Trends are negligible at the cycle level; however, minor linear drifts appear over multi-cycle spans (e.g., −0.004/pt in ref 2 & 3), likely due to residual non-stationarity rather than true trend. Curvature is near-zero except in ref 3 where slight convexity appears in the rising edge of later cycles—likely an artifact of window length or edge effects. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates show full cycles at both ends. Acceptable variation includes: (i) ±0.1 shift in plateau/trough levels, (ii) occasional extra micro-spikes (≤3 consecutive points, amplitude ≤0.3), (iii) minor asymmetry in rise/fall steepness, and (iv) very shallow monotonic drift (<0.005/pt) over ≥200 points.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (1P) excerpt showing one clean, textbook square-wave cycle: flat baseline at 0, sharp drop to −0.5, brief trough, sharp rise to +1.0, long plateau, then symmetric fall back to baseline. No noise spikes; perfectly stable levels. Idealized morphology with no drift or distortion.

Three-cycle (3P) excerpt with clear repetition of the square-wave motif. Plateaus slightly lower (~+0.95) than ref 0; troughs deeper (−0.6 to −0.7). Contains moderate high-frequency micro-spikes (especially around indices 825–840 and 915–930), but core step-plateau structure remains intact. Very slight positive slope (+0.0013/pt) across the window—likely benign residual trend.

Three-cycle (3P) excerpt mirroring ref 1’s motif but with inverted drift (−0.0043/pt) and slightly higher plateau (~+1.04). Troughs are shallower (−0.5 to −0.6). Micro-spikes present but less frequent than ref 1; one notable double-spike near index 1740. Overall morphology highly consistent with ref 1; differences attributable to natural variation within normal regime.

Five-cycle (5P) excerpt showing extended repetition of the motif. Plateaus and troughs align closely with refs 1–2. Contains more frequent micro-spikes and subtle curvature in rising edges (curvature ≈0.35), possibly due to window length or edge smoothing. One minor irregularity near index 2535 (compressed cycle), but still recognizable as normal. Slight negative drift (−0.0042/pt) persists.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries matching a single clean cycle (e.g., short windows or isolated anomalies). Use reference 1 for queries with mild upward drift and moderate spikes; reference 2 for downward drift scenarios. Reference 3 is best for long-window queries (>300 pts) where multi-cycle consistency and drift behavior matter most. When query morphology shows strong symmetry and zero noise, align with ref 0; when it shows micro-spikes but preserved step-plateau shape, match to refs 1–3. Avoid using ref 3’s curvature as a normative feature—it appears only in longest window and may be artifactual.
uncertainties: Whether the micro-spikes are intrinsic normal jitter or low-level contamination (but their recurrence across all train candidates suggests normality)
Exact tolerance for drift magnitude: catalog shows slopes from −0.0043 to +0.0013, but unknown if steeper drifts would be anomalous
Boundary effects in 5P window may inflate curvature estimate; true normal curvature likely near zero
Amplitude variation (1.44–1.78) spans ~25%—unclear if values outside this band are always anomalous without ground truth
